## Product Vision

Build AI-powered support ticket management system. Core product: ticket CRUD + lifecycle. AI-native feature: RAG Q&A over ticket history, designed in from start, not bolted on.

Assessment focus: spec-driven development, grounded AI answers, documented AI mistakes caught during build.

---

## Core Ticket Features (Must Have)

- Create ticket
- List tickets
- View ticket detail
- Update title, description, priority, assignee
- Add comments
- Keyword search
- Filter by status
- Persist to database; data survives restart
- Backend input validation
- UI shows meaningful validation/error messages

---

## Ticket State Machine (Backend-Enforced)

Valid transitions only:

| From | To |
|------|-----|
| OPEN | IN_PROGRESS, CANCELLED |
| IN_PROGRESS | RESOLVED, CANCELLED |
| RESOLVED | CLOSED |
| CLOSED | (terminal) |
| CANCELLED | (terminal) |

Invalid transitions rejected by backend (e.g. CLOSED → OPEN, RESOLVED → OPEN, CANCELLED → OPEN). State-machine integration tests required.

---

## Data Model Hints (for spec)

Ticket fields: title, description, priority, assignee, status, category (RAG metadata), comments, resolution notes.

Comment thread per ticket. Ticket ID format example: `TKT-1001`.

---

## RAG / AI Assistant Requirements

### Purpose

Natural-language Q&A over ticket history. Single retrieval → generate flow. Not autonomous agent — no ticket creation, notifications, or tool chaining.

### Example User Questions

- "Have we seen payment failures before?"
- "What was the resolution for ticket TKT-1001?"
- "What are the common causes of shipment tracking issues?"
- "Show me similar resolved tickets."
- "Which high-priority tickets are related to payment?"

### Ingestion Pipeline

```
Ticket (description + comments + resolution notes)
  → Knowledge documents
  → Chunk
  → Embeddings
  → Vector store
```

Metadata per document: `ticketId`, `status`, `priority`, `assignee`, `category`.

Re-ingest on ticket update or close. Embeddings must not go stale.

### API

`POST /api/ai/ask`

```json
{ "question": "What caused previous payment failures?" }
```

Response must include grounded answer + cited ticket ID(s).

### Grounding & Guardrails

- Answer only from retrieved ticket context
- No fallback to general LLM knowledge for support questions
- No relevant tickets → explicit "no relevant tickets found" (no fabricated plausible answers)
- Cite specific ticket(s) used in every in-scope answer

### Retrieval Config (Must Be Configurable)

- Top-K
- Similarity threshold
- Chunking strategy (document choice + rationale for ticket data)
- Embedding model choice (local Ollama vs cloud; cost/latency/quality tradeoff documented)

---

## Tech Stack Constraints

| Layer | Choice |
|-------|--------|
| Backend | Java 21, Spring Boot, Spring AI |
| Database | PostgreSQL or H2 |
| Vector store | PGVector or Chroma |
| Embeddings | Embedding model (choice documented) |
| API | REST |
| Frontend | React/Next.js or equivalent |
| Dev tooling | Cursor / GitHub Copilot / Kiro with spec-driven workflow |

---

## Non-Functional Requirements

- No secrets committed to repo
- Backend validation on all inputs
- Deterministic logic (state machine) + probabilistic logic (RAG) both tested
- RAG output review for hallucination / ungrounded answers
- Token optimization via Graphify, Caveman, Codebase-memory MCP, prompt caching

---

## AI Engineering Hygiene (Project Setup)

Rules/skills/commands for: Java Spring Boot, testing, API standards, RAG/vector store, documentation, code review, spec review, test generation, RAG hallucination review.

Prompt history saved under `.specstory/history/` and `docs/prompt-history.md`.

Document at least one meaningful AI mistake caught (wrong code or ungrounded RAG answer).

---

## Acceptance Criteria Checklist (Definition of Done)

**Tickets:** create, list, view, update fields, change assignee, add comments, search, status filter — all from UI.

**State machine:** valid transitions work; invalid rejected by backend; integration tests pass.

**Persistence:** data survives restart; backend validation works; UI shows errors.

**RAG:** embeddings stored in vector store; re-ingest on update; top-K + threshold configurable.

**AI ask:** grounded answer with ticket citations for in-scope questions; honest no-match response for out-of-scope.

**Docs:** chunking strategy + embedding model choice justified in `architecture.md`.

**Security:** no committed secrets.

**Process:** at least one documented AI mistake caught during development.

---

## Open Spec Decisions (Clarify in spec phase)

- PostgreSQL vs H2 for dev/prod
- PGVector vs Chroma
- Local (Ollama) vs cloud embedding/LLM
- Ticket category taxonomy (free text vs enum)
- Assignee model (user entity vs string)
- Citation format in API response (inline IDs vs structured sources array)
- Default top-K and similarity threshold values
- Chunk size / overlap for ticket comments vs description

Want these folded into `spec/requirements.md` draft next?

**Question:** When a ticket moves to RESOLVED, how must resolution notes be captured?

Resolution notes feed both ticket detail and RAG indexing — this choice drives data model, UI, validation on status change, and what gets embedded.

**Recommended:** Option B — A dedicated `resolution` field is required when status becomes RESOLVED. That gives a clear field for agents, a hard validation rule on transition, and a stable RAG document boundary separate from the comment thread.

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| A | No dedicated field — resolution lives only in comments |
| B | Dedicated resolution field required when status becomes RESOLVED |
| C | Optional dedicated resolution field — indexed when present, not required on transition |
| D | Resolution is a comment with a special type/tag (e.g., `RESOLUTION`) |
| Short | Provide a different short answer (≤5 words) |

Reply with option letter (e.g., `B`), say `yes` / `recommended` to accept B, or give your own short answer.

**Question:** How should ticket content be split into RAG knowledge documents?

Chunk boundaries drive ingestion pipeline, chunking config, citation granularity, and re-index scope.

**Recommended:** Option B — Separate indexed units per description, each comment, and resolution field. Best retrieval precision; citations can point to exact source section; partial re-index on comment add possible.

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| A | One knowledge document per ticket — all content concatenated |
| B | Separate indexed units per description, each comment, and resolution field |
| C | One document per ticket with automatic sub-chunking at fixed token size |
| D | One document per ticket with sub-chunking at comment boundaries only |
| Short | Provide a different short answer (≤5 words) |

---

**Question:** Which ticket changes must trigger re-indexing of knowledge documents?

With per-section units from Q2, trigger rules define what gets re-embedded vs metadata-only update — directly affects ingestion jobs and stale-answer tests.

**Recommended:** Option B — Re-embed only when searchable text changes (description edit, new/edited comment, resolution set/changed); metadata-only changes (status, priority, assignee, category) update unit metadata without re-embedding text. Efficient, matches unit model, still keeps filters accurate.

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| A | Any ticket mutation re-embeds all units for that ticket |
| B | Re-embed on searchable text change; metadata-only changes update unit metadata without re-embedding |
| C | Re-embed only on create, new comment, and transition to RESOLVED |
| D | Re-embed on every mutation including terminal status (CLOSED/CANCELLED), even if text unchanged |
| Short | Provide a different short answer (≤5 words) |

Reply with option letter, `yes` / `recommended`, or your own short answer.
